items.title: Multi-omics insights into Citrus essential oils: linking biosynthesis, molecular mechanisms, and applications in food, health, and agriculture
items.summary: Citrus essential oils (CEOs) are complex mixtures of volatile terpenoids with potential applications in food preservation, health-related products, and sustainable agriculture. However, variations in chemical composition, physicochemical instability, and limited mechanistic evidence constrain their standardization and practical utilization. This review critically examines CEO biosynthesis and applications from a multi-omics perspective, focusing on essential oils derived from species of the genus Citrus. items.title: Phytochemical Composition, Bioactivities, and Medicinal Value of Salvia nemorosa L.
items.summary: Salvia nemorosa L. (Lamiaceae) is a perennial herb native mainly to Europe and Western Asia and has a fragmented but longstanding record of ethnomedicinal use. Although widely distributed, it remains a relatively underexplored member of the Salvia genus. Recent investigations have revealed that S. nemorosa is a rich source of bioactive secondary metabolites, particularly phenolic acids, flavonoids, diterpenoids, triterpenoids, megastigmane glycosides, and volatile terpenoids. Among these, rosmarinic acid, sagerinic acid, and caffeoylquinic acids are predominant constituents contributing to its pronounced antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities. items.title: Solvent‐Dependent Metabolomic Profiling of Bioactive Compounds in Dried Ginger Rhizome Using Gas Chromatography–Mass Spectrometry
items.summary: ABSTRACT Ginger rhizome ( Zingiber officinale Roscoe ) is a chemically complex natural product matrix in which extraction conditions strongly influence the observed chemical composition. Six commonly used solvents, including methanol, ethanol, acetonitrile, acetone, ethyl acetate, and dichloromethane, were compared using four independent extraction replicates prepared from the same homogenized batch. items.summary: Salvia rosmarinus, formerly known as Rosmarinus officinalis, is a medicinal plant known as one of the sources of abietane-type diterpenoids. The largest family of chemical constituents from the Salvia genus is abietanes and rearranged abietanes. Since 1976, 365 of the 545 known diterpenoids have been recognized as abietane diterpenoids. Carnosic acid, carnosol, rosmanol, epirosmanol, and their derivatives are among the bioactive abietanes that have gained much attention because of the wide spectrum of pharmacological activities. items.title: Floral Volatile Organic Compounds of Chinese Cymbidium Orchids: From Biosynthesis and Function to Genetic Regulation
items.summary: Chinese Cymbidium orchids (Cymbidium spp.), collectively known as Guolan, are highly valued ornamental plants renowned for their elegant and persistent floral fragrance.
